nocalltoerror.description: A NoCallToError is triggered when a method is explicitly prohibited in a cryptographic usage pattern, yet it has been invoked. CrySL rules may specify that certain method calls should not occur under specific conditions, such as restricting init() for certain algorithms that do not require explicit initialization. This error signals that the cryptographic implementation does not follow secure guidelines and may introduce security weaknesses.

examples.misuse:
The following call should never be made:
SecretKey sharedKey = keAgreement.generateSecret(symmetricKeyAlgorithm);
examples.solution:
Instead use 
byte[] sharedSecretBuffer = keyAgreement.generateSecret();
or 
byte[] sharedSecretBuffer = new byte[1024];
generateSecret(sharedSecretBuffer, offset);

examples.misuse:
The following constructor must be called before the privateKey and publicKey can be returned:
KeyPair kp = new KeyPair(PrublicKey publicKey, PrivateKey, privateKey);
